Some lesions were associated with ulceration and bleeding. The patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery without prenatal care. No history of environmental or hazardous substance exposure. Paternal family history was unremarkable; maternal family history was unknown.

Physical examination revealed:- Numerous bright red macules, papules, and plaques ranging in size from 1.0 × 1.0 mm to 2.2 × 2.3 cm- Many lesions had hemorrhagic crust and dark scale- Retrognathia- Thickened maxillary frenulum- Anterior ankyloglossia

Laboratory Tests:- Complete blood cell count: normal- Metabolic panel: normalImaging Studies:- Abdominal ultrasonography: normal- Brain MRI (at 4 months):   * 7 × 5 × 6-mm enhancing nodule along posterior temporal dural surface  * Enhancing exophytic soft tissue polyps in neck and scalp  * Mild hypogenesis/dysgenesis of corpus callosum  * Evidence of prior pineal hemorrhagePathology:- Histopathology showed upper dermal lobulated capillary proliferation- Immunohistochemistry results:  * CD31: positive  * Smooth muscle actin (SMA): positive  * D2-40: negative  * GLUT-1: negativeGenetic Testing:- Negative for ATR, BRAF, FLT4, GNA14, HRAS, KDR, KRAS, and NRAS genes
